neighboring_unit_entries.title: Extending partial-interval phases to use exponent-pair theory
neighboring_unit_entries.why_material: To remove the full-interval assumption, the source constructs a smooth extension of the phase from [a,b] to [M/2,M] using a monomial derivative model plus a correcting polynomial, argues that derivative conditions persist, and then invokes an interval-restriction lemma at logarithmic cost.

related_synthesis_entries.claim: A strong estimate on one natural scale range becomes a reusable exponent-pair result only after complementary estimates cover missing ranges, the B-process handles dual large scales, and a controlled phase extension removes the full-interval assumption.
related_synthesis_entries.limit: Several steps are cited from established exponent-pair theory and the construction assumes its derivative and monomial-approximation hypotheses.
